description: Re-state a time in another timezone, DST-correct for the date in question. Use this instead of adding a remembered offset: offsets change with the calendar, and the hour either side of a changeover is where guesses go wrong. Give `time` with an offset for an exact instant, or without one plus `from` for a wall-clock reading in a named zone.

format.description: Token pattern for `formatted`, rendered in `to`. Defaults to ISO with offset.

from.description: Zone the wall-clock `time` was read in. Required when `time` has no offset. IANA name such as "UTC", "Europe/Berlin", "America/New_York" or "Asia/Kolkata".

time.description: ISO 8601. With an offset ("2026-03-29T01:30:00+01:00", "...Z") it pins an instant. Without one ("2026-03-29T01:30:00") it is a wall-clock reading and `from` is required.

to.description: Zone to convert into. IANA name such as "UTC", "Europe/Berlin", "America/New_York" or "Asia/Kolkata".

name: convert_timezone

dstTransition.description: True when the instant is within an hour of a DST changeover in `to` -- the case where a guessed offset is most likely wrong. Trust `local` and `offset` over any assumption.

formatted.description: The requested `format`, rendered. Same value as the text content.

from.description: Zone the input was interpreted in: `from`, or "offset in input".

iso.description: The instant as ISO 8601 UTC. Use this for machine timestamps.

local.description: Host-local clock reading as ISO 8601 with its real offset, e.g. 2026-08-20T14:31:02.625+02:00.

timezone.description: IANA zone that `local` and `offset` are stated in, e.g. "Europe/Berlin".

utc.description: UTC clock reading. Identical to `iso` in this version.

title: Convert a time between timezones
